issues.legal_issue: A land-ceiling law previously invalidated for inconsistency with fundamental rights can acquire retrospective force through its inclusion in the constitutional schedule without being reenacted by the State Legislature.
material_facts: The land-ceiling law had previously been struck down because provisions concerning the ceiling and compensation violated the equality guarantee.
A subsequent constitutional amendment included the law in the Ninth Schedule, where Article 31-B protected scheduled laws from invalidity based on inconsistency with Part III of the Constitution.
The challengers argued that the law was void from inception and required reenactment by the State Legislature.
issues.conclusion: The law was protected retrospectively from the date of its enactment and did not require reenactment by the State Legislature.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-B, read with the Ninth Schedule, cures defects based on inconsistency with Part III, including where a law had already been held invalid; its express retrospective effect means the law operates from its enactment after inclusion in the Schedule. A State Legislature cannot itself cure a defect arising from violation of Part III. The Court relied on State of Maharashtra v. Patilchand, Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of Madhya Pradesh, M.P.V. Sundararamier & Co. v. State of Andhra Pradesh, and State of Uttar Pradesh v. H.H. Maharaja Brijendra Singh.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_ceiling: A constitutional challenge is brought against a law that limits agricultural land holdings.
predicates.previously_invalidated_for_fundamental_r: A court had previously invalidated the law because it was inconsistent with a fundamental right.
predicates.later_included_in_constitutional_schedul: A later constitutional amendment placed the law in a schedule that protects listed laws from the relevant fundamental-rights challenge.

issues.definition: When a challenged land-ceiling law was previously invalidated for fundamental-rights inconsistency and is later placed in the protective constitutional schedule, it operates from its original enactment without State reenactment.

issues.legal_issue: A State Legislature has competence to impose ceilings on agricultural land, acquire surplus land, and distribute it to advance agrarian reform and reduce concentration of land ownership.
material_facts: The law imposed ceilings on agricultural land holdings and provided for acquisition of land held beyond the ceiling.
The acquired surplus land was to be distributed to landless and other persons to reduce disparities in land ownership and advance the stated common-good objectives.
Persons whose surplus land was acquired were entitled to compensation.
The challengers argued that the State Legislature lacked power to enact this scheme under the relevant legislative entries.
issues.conclusion: The State Legislature was competent to enact the land-ceiling scheme: the legislation fell within the broad scope of the State's land-related legislative field, and acquisition of surplus land was supported by the concurrent power over acquisition and requisitioning of property.
issues.legal_principle: Legislative-list entries describing a subject are construed broadly, and the land entry encompasses a wide range of legislation concerning rights in or over land, including agrarian reform and measures to improve land use. Although acquisition is not directly covered by the land entry, the State may acquire surplus land under that entry read with the concurrent entry on acquisition and requisitioning of property, including to advance Article 39(b) and (c). The Court relied on Sri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, Atma Ram v. State of Punjab, Sonapur Tea Co. Ltd. v. Mst. Mazirunnessa, and State of Maharashtra v. Patilchand.

predicates.challenge_to_state_legislative_competenc: A challenge claims that a State Legislature lacks power to enact a land-reform measure.
predicates.law_limits_agricultural_land_holdings: The law sets a maximum area of agricultural land that a person or family may hold.
predicates.surplus_land_is_acquired_for_redistribut: The law provides for acquiring land above the ceiling so it can be distributed to landless or other persons.
predicates.acquisition_is_compensated: The law provides compensation to persons whose surplus land is acquired.

issues.definition: A State Legislature has competence to enact the challenged land-reform scheme when it limits agricultural holdings and provides for compensated acquisition of surplus land for redistribution.
